request.spec:
A sheet may name a parent sheet (settings, SETTING_CHANGED key=parent value=<sheet id>; not
dated). A sheet cannot be its own parent, nor name a sheet that has this sheet as an ancestor; and
the parent must be a sheet that exists (has been loaded); each is refused with an error on the
settings. When a grade has no rate in force on a date on this sheet, the parent's rate for that grade
and date is used, then the parent's parent, up to three levels up. Show the parent sheet id on the
screen (nothing when none).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A sheet may name a parent sheet (settings, SETTING_CHANGED key=parent value=<sheet id>; not
dated). A sheet cannot be its own parent, nor name a sheet that has this sheet as an ancestor; and
the parent must be a sheet that exists (has been loaded); each is refused with an error on the
settings. When a grade has no rate in force on a date on this sheet, the parent's rate for that grade
and date is used, then the parent's parent, up to three levels up. Show the parent sheet id on the
screen (nothing when none).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A sheet can now name a parent sheet, and grades with no rate of their own fall back to the parent's rates, up to three levels up. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How it works**
- **Storing the parent:** a new migration `V65__sheet_parent.sql` adds a `parent_id` column to `sheet_setting`, set up the same way as the existing pot column. It's saved through the normal settings form, and the audit line is `SETTING_CHANGED … key=parent value=<id>`. Leaving the field blank clears the parent. Changing the parent also writes ROLLUP and TOTALS lines for figures that move, like any other settings change.
- **Refusals:** all three show `settings-error` and write nothing. The checks are in `ValidateSettings`:
  - naming the sheet itself;
  - naming a sheet that has never been loaded (`Sheets.exists`);
  - naming a sheet that has this sheet as an ancestor (`Settings.isAncestor`).
- **Rates on the server:** `Rates.pct` uses the sheet's own rate in force on that date. If there isn't one, it tries the parent, then the parent's parent, up to three levels. Claim dues, rollups and statements all go through `Rates.pct`, so they all pick up inherited rates.
- **Rates on the screen:** the front end works out dues itself, so it needs the parent sheets' rates too. A new endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{id}/rates/inherited`, returns them nearest parent first. `useRates` combines them with the sheet's own rates, and `rateOn` checks each level in order. The rate list still shows only the sheet's own rates.
- **Display:** the parent id appears in `sheet-parent` next to Archived, and in the settings panel as `setting-parent-current` with a `setting-parent` input. Both are empty when there's no parent.

**Behaviour in as-of views**
- The parent setting isn't dated, so the as-of view still shows the parent as it is now. Scenario 3 expects this.
- Inherited rates don't show up in an as-of view. That view rebuilds only the sheet itself, so the parent's rates aren't there and grades without their own rate show n/a. That's what the test expects at that point, but it means as-of figures never use the parent's rates.
